utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what I'm saying because there was no need for them to fire. And the other combat position was in operation one day; it is visible from Zarkovica. And that is why it wasn't well placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, this other position, the ZIS, Z-I-S, cannon position, near the Ivo Vojnovic Street, how many shells were fired from that cannon on the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I think it was about 170.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I see. 170. Now, that cannon, at that position, did it open fire in November as well, November 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I really can't say with certainty. All I know is about the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That cannon, once again, apart from the 6th of December 1991, did it open fire at any other time in the period from the 1st of October to the 31st of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I will have to give you a slightly longer answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But please try and keep it brief, as brief as possible. Time is of the essence.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Well, then you won't get the right picture. We had two combat positions, and we had 200 pieces for two cannons. On that day, since there was shelling and an all-out infantry and tank attack, we were forced to use that amount of ammunition, whereas the other didn't use even four. Because we had to keep all the shells except for an infantry attack in order to prevent them taking control of Srdj and entering town. And that is why that cannon fired that many shells. So of the 200 shells they had, practically none remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, you either don't understand me, or you seem to be swerving and giving broader answers. But you're not answering my specific question. We have heard that the cannon placed in Ivo Vojnovic Street on the 6th of December, that it fired 170 shells. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: My question is now, apart from the 6th of December, in the period from the 1st of October to the 31st of December 1991, did that gun ever open fire again?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: No, sir, it was not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You are claiming that the action of that gun for the period of three months was only on one day, was limited to one day, the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Yes. But I have to add very briefly again --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, concerning the positions of mortars, near the auto camp?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... add to his response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very briefly, again, you were going to add something, Mr. Negodic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I want to say to this gentleman, and for your information, Your Honour, that so many shells were used because directly looking at the town and the Srdj fortress, we were facing a large tank attack. And that's why we used so many shells. We were not able to respond to the shelling of the town before the 6th of December, before we did not have adequate range for a 130- and 122-millimetre gun, and we would have been wasting our ammunition unless we approached and came closer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the position of that mortar near the SDK building or the Dubrovkinja building as it was also known, for how long was that position in existence before the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: If you're asking me about dates, I cannot answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about dates. Tell me, 15 days back, 20 days back.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: As soon as we withdrew to the area of the town, that firing position was established. And on several times, and on several occasions, fire was opened from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you are telling me that fire was opened on several occasions from that firing position, can you tell me how many times before the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Seven, eight, ten times.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you perhaps remember any dates?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But do you remember, for instance, how many shells were fired on each occasion from that position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: Who would be able to tell you that after 13 years I wonder. All I know is that we were economising, except on the 6th of December when we used up all the shells we had from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And do you know how many shells from that position, after firing from that position remained unused on each occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. But we always tried to save some for the rainy day. And that rainy day came on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you are only aware of the Lazaret position. You know that 12 remained and that you used around 10.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the number.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Continued]
utterances.text: I know that four shells were used every time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the evidence was that 16 shells were used, and 4 remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's correct, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said, Your Honour. But it was not recorded properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the examination-in-chief, you explained that mortars near Lazaret, 100 metres away from Old Town, had to be there to prevent any attack, any breakthrough of the infantry towards the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The witness didn't say the mortars near Lazaret were a hundred metres away. He gave an indication more than hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that is correct, Mr. Rodic. But it also occurs to me that the time has been reached where we must allow your client to leave or he won't get back to the Detention Centre. So we will have to adjourn for the day. The question arises, which you no doubt anticipate from me, how much longer would you expect to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in my estimate, if I try to be brief, I believe I would not use up all of the second session tomorrow. Sometime in the second session I could be done with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Rodic, you are exceeding our estimation of the time you would justifiably take. Could we put to you that you should, over the evening break, give close attention to finishing by the end of the first session tomorrow. Look at your questions again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will do my level best, but I'm asking also for your understanding because we have here the only representative of the Croatian Army whose examination-in-chief lasted two full days, and we the Defence had one day, one whole day today and a little over 40 minutes on Friday. I will continue to make my cross-examination as brief as I can, but I hope that you can appreciate our situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, as you are well aware, we do appreciate it, Mr. Rodic, and that's why we have been quiet and letting you get on with it as much as possible. And we do appreciate that your questioning has been quite direct. But there have been times when you've wandered off on to issues that are not central to the case, and time has been lost. So we ask you overnight to look again at your proposed questions to make sure you are dealing only with the issues that matter in this case. We will adjourn now and resume tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
